chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man prostrates and then intends to rise, he should not press his hands into the ground, but rather spread his palms without placing his seat (buttocks) on the ground."
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim rise from prostration during prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, refines the physical mechanics of rising from sujood by prohibiting the forceful pressing of palms (ijnan) into the earth. It emphasizes a graceful, controlled movement where the palms are spread lightly to support the body while the buttocks remain elevated, reflecting the Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt in maintaining dignity and precision during prayer.
